match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the adjusted trial balance: the reducing balance loans card is a mathematics topic, and the balance sheet card covers a financial statement at one date, not a trial balance prepared after balance day adjustments.

draft.title: The adjusted trial balance
card: A trial balance lists every ledger account balance in a debit column and a credit column. If the records are correct, the two columns have the same total.
An adjusted trial balance is prepared after the balance day adjustments have been posted to the ledger. It shows each account's balance once the adjustments are included.
The columns should still be equal. If they are not, an error has been made, such as posting only one side of an adjusting entry.

The adjusted balances are used to prepare the end-of-period reports: the income statement and the balance sheet. Revenue and expense accounts feed the income statement. Asset, liability and equity accounts feed the balance sheet.
draft.remember: The adjusted trial balance has the final balances for the reports, and its columns must still be equal.

a.q: Why is an adjusted trial balance prepared before the end-of-period reports?
opts: It shows account balances that include the adjustments
It replaces the need to post adjustments to the ledger
It proves that no errors are in the accounts
It lists only the accounts that were adjusted
a.why: The reports need balances that include the adjustments, and the adjusted trial balance gives them. It does not replace posting the adjustments. Equal columns also do not prove there are no errors, because some mistakes keep the totals equal.
a.clue: Think about which balances the reports should use.

b.q: Priya's adjusted trial balance for her bakery in Ballarat has debits of $58,400 and credits of $57,900. What is the most likely cause?
opts: One side of an adjusting entry was not posted
The reports were prepared before the trial balance
The adjustments were made in the wrong period
Some accounts were left out of the income statement
b.why: The columns should be equal, so a $500 gap points to an error such as posting only one side of an adjusting entry. The timing of adjustments would not on its own make the columns unequal. The income statement is prepared after the trial balance, so it cannot cause the gap.
b.clue: Each adjusting entry has a debit and a credit.

a.best: It shows account balances that include the adjustments

b.best: One side of an adjusting entry was not posted

problems.detail: The remember line says the columns 'must' still be equal, but the card says they 'should' still be equal. The card also notes they may not be equal if an error was made. Using 'should' would match the card.
